measures.revision: 09/10/2026 – The description part was updated and recommendations have been revised to reflect the change in the risk area.

properties.title: EASA CZIB-2026-08-R3: Airspace of Jordan

measures.airspace: FIR Amman (OJAC), all altitudes and flight levels.
measures.recommendation: Air operators should: Take potential risks into account when operating in the affected airspace; Ensure that an up-do-date risk assessment is in place together with a high level of contingency planning for their operations and be ready for short notice instructions from State authorities. measures.revision: 14/10/2026 – The validity of the CZIB was extended until 16 November 2026. The content and recommendations have been revised to reflect the change in the risk level.

properties.title: EASA CZIB-2026-07R3: Airspace of the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman

measures.airspace: All altitudes and flight levels in the airspace of:- Bahrain (Bahrain FIR – OBBB), - Kuwait (Kuwait FIR – OKAC),- Qatar (Doha FIR – OTDF), - United Arab Emirates (Emirates FIR – OMAE), and - Oman (FIR Muscat - OOMM).
measures.recommendation: Air operators should: Not operate at all altitudes and flight levels within the airspace over the waters of the Persian Gulf within FIR Bahrain (OBBB), FIR Kuwait (OKAC), FIR Doha (OTDF), FIR Emirates (OMAE), except to the extent necessary for arrivals at or departures from aerodromes within the affected FIRs. measures.revision: 30/09/2026 – The validity of the CZIB was extended until 16 November 2026. No changes to the content or recommendations have been made.

sources.publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Travelers' Health
sources.licence: US public domain (CDC asks for credit and a no-endorsement disclaimer)

measures.summary: The Kenyan Ministry of Health has confirmed an imported case, as well as other linked cases, of Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus in Nairobi, Kenya.

properties.title: CDC Level 2 (Practice Enhanced Precautions): Global Polio

sources.publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Travelers' Health
sources.licence: US public domain (CDC asks for credit and a no-endorsement disclaimer)

measures.summary: Some international destinations have circulating poliovirus. Before any international travel, make sure you are up to date on your polio vaccines.

properties.title: CDC Level 1 (Practice Usual Precautions): Hepatitis A in Canada

sources.publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Travelers' Health
sources.licence: US public domain (CDC asks for credit and a no-endorsement disclaimer)

measures.summary: Manitoba, Canada is currently experiencing a hepatitis A virus (HAV) outbreak. HAV is contagious and spreads through close person-to-person contact and by eating contaminated food or drink.

properties.title: CDC Level 1 (Practice Usual Precautions): Hepatitis A in Costa Rica

sources.publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Travelers' Health
sources.licence: US public domain (CDC asks for credit and a no-endorsement disclaimer)

measures.summary: There is an outbreak of hepatitis A (HAV) in Costa Rica. Most cases have been reported in San José province.

properties.title: CDC Level 2 (Practice Enhanced Precautions): Malaria in Mayotte

sources.publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Travelers' Health
sources.licence: US public domain (CDC asks for credit and a no-endorsement disclaimer)

measures.summary: Increased cases of malaria have been reported in Mayotte. Malaria is spread by the bite of infected mosquitoes.

properties.title: CDC Level 2 (Practice Enhanced Precautions): Malaria in Yemen

sources.publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Travelers' Health
sources.licence: US public domain (CDC asks for credit and a no-endorsement disclaimer)

measures.summary: Increased cases of malaria have been reported in Yemen, including in areas that were previously considered low-risk.

properties.title: CDC Level 1 (Practice Usual Precautions): Global Measles

sources.publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Travelers' Health
sources.licence: US public domain (CDC asks for credit and a no-endorsement disclaimer)

measures.summary: Measles cases are rising in many countries around the world. All international travelers should be fully vaccinated against measles with the measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine, according to CDC's measles vaccination recommendations for international travel.

properties.title: CDC Level 2 (Practice Enhanced Precautions): Meningococcal Disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo

sources.publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Travelers' Health
sources.licence: US public domain (CDC asks for credit and a no-endorsement disclaimer)

measures.summary: There is an outbreak of meningococcal disease in the Mangembo Health Zone of Kongo Central Province. The best way to protect yourself is to get meningococcal vaccination.

properties.title: CDC Level 1 (Practice Usual Precautions): Paratyphoid Fever in Yemen

sources.publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Travelers' Health
sources.licence: US public domain (CDC asks for credit and a no-endorsement disclaimer)

measures.summary: Cases of paratyphoid fever are being reported in returning travelers from Yemen. You can prevent paratyphoid fever by practicing safe eating and drinking habits.

properties.title: CDC Level 1 (Practice Usual Precautions): Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever in Mexico

sources.publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Travelers' Health
sources.licence: US public domain (CDC asks for credit and a no-endorsement disclaimer)

measures.summary: Illness and death due to Rocky Mountain spotted fever (RMSF) have been reported in the northern region of Mexico along the U.S. border, particularly in Baja California, Sonora, Chihuahua, Coahuila, and Nuevo León.

properties.title: CDC Level 2 (Practice Enhanced Precautions): Yellow Fever in Colombia

sources.publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Travelers' Health
sources.licence: US public domain (CDC asks for credit and a no-endorsement disclaimer)

measures.summary: An increased number of cases of yellow fever have been reported in Colombia.

properties.title: CDC Level 2 (Practice Enhanced Precautions): Yellow Fever in Burkina Faso, Côte d’Ivoire, and Ghana

sources.publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Travelers' Health
sources.licence: US public domain (CDC asks for credit and a no-endorsement disclaimer)

measures.summary: There are outbreaks of yellow fever in the Nando Region of Burkina Faso, Bounkani Region of Côte d’Ivoire, and the Upper West Region of Ghana. Travelers to these regions should take steps to prevent yellow fever by getting vaccinated at least 10 days before travel and taking steps to prevent mosquito bites.

properties.title: CDC Level 2 (Practice Enhanced Precautions): Zika in Indonesia

sources.publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Travelers' Health
sources.licence: US public domain (CDC asks for credit and a no-endorsement disclaimer)

measures.summary: Cases of Zika are being reported in returning travelers from Bali, Indonesia. All travelers to Bali should take steps to prevent mosquito bites and sexual transmission of Zika virus during and after travel.
